skill.name: address-github-comments
skill.description: Review and address comments on an open GitHub pull request with the GitHub CLI.
skill.summary: Turn pull request feedback into confirmed code changes and clear follow-up comments.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Pull request feedback can become difficult to track. This skill organizes comments, plans fixes, applies approved changes, and reports completion.
actual_capabilities: Checks GitHub CLI authentication before starting the workflow.
Fetches comments for the current branch pull request.
Organizes comments and review threads into actionable items.
Proposes a fix for each selected item.
Applies approved code changes for review feedback.
Posts a pull request comment after changes are complete.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI and repository access.
Does not provide a built-in script for listing individual review threads.
Does not replace project tests or environment-specific validation.
Requires clarification when permissions, inputs, or success criteria are missing.

use_cases.title: Resolve Author Feedback
use_cases.description: Collect reviewer comments, choose priorities, implement approved fixes, and report completion on the pull request.

use_cases.title: Track Requested Changes
use_cases.description: Convert review threads into a clear checklist and verify that each selected request receives a response.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Repository Reviews
use_cases.description: Triage many comments before assigning or applying focused changes across an active pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Pull Request Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Check GitHub CLI authentication, then show comments for the current branch pull request. Do not change files.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Review Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: List each pull request comment, explain the requested change, and propose a fix. Ask before editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured planning for a manageable review.

prompt_templates.title: Address Selected Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Address comments [COMMENT REFERENCES]. Read surrounding code, apply focused changes, run relevant validation, and summarize results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation after the user selects comments.

prompt_templates.title: Manage a Large Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage all review threads by priority and dependency. Present an execution order, wait for approval, then address the approved group.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coordination for a pull request with many threads.

output_examples.input: Inspect comments on the pull request for my current branch.
output: Two request code changes, and one asks for clarification.

output_examples.input: Plan fixes for the error handling and test coverage comments.
output: Error handling: preserve the original error and add context at the service boundary.
Test coverage: add failure-path coverage for rejected requests.
Approval is required before editing files.

output_examples.input: Address the approved review comments and summarize the result.
output: The two approved changes were applied.
The remaining discussion was not modified.
A completion response is ready for the pull request.

best_practices: Read surrounding code before interpreting a reviewer comment.
Request user confirmation before addressing a large set of comments.
Run relevant validation before reporting a comment as addressed.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every suggestion without checking project context.
Do not start changes before confirming GitHub CLI authentication.
Do not mark feedback resolved when validation has not completed.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks authentication and can guide an interactive login when needed.

faq.question: Which pull request does it inspect?
faq.answer: The workflow inspects the pull request associated with the current branch.

faq.question: Will it change files immediately?
faq.answer: It first reviews comments and proposes fixes. Large comment sets require user confirmation before changes.

faq.question: Can it list individual review threads?
faq.answer: The basic workflow shows pull request comments. Detailed thread listing requires an available custom script or another GitHub CLI query.

faq.question: Does it run project tests?
faq.answer: The skill requires environment-specific validation, but the documented workflow does not prescribe a specific test command.

faq.question: Can it post a completion comment?
faq.answer: Yes. It can post a fixed completion message after approved changes are applied.
